# ramen-agents

> ramen-agents is an open-source (Apache-2.0), free AI agent team for a small business: it finds leads, researches the
> market and prices service packages, each with a ready-to-send email that your team sends, and a local dashboard shows
> the agents working. It is for founders and small agencies with a Mac and big plans, and it costs nothing to
> run: free model tiers and keyless search, no card anywhere. A fence in the code stops any agent from creating
> accounts, spending money or collecting personal data.

Running in production since late September 2026: 800+ leads found by the agents, 25 service packages priced and published, and 35 actions the fence refused.

## What it is

- A family of web agents (The CEO, Lead Gen, Package Designer, Research Analyst, Scout), a Validator that checks every
  write against the owner's rules, and a local Next.js dashboard drawn as a small pixel world.
- Each agent is a folder with a `config.toml` and a `persona.md` in plain English; one Python program (`bot`) runs them.
- No agent sends email: packages carry a ready-to-send email, and your team sends it.

## Best for

- Bootstrapped B2B lead finding: small businesses with a gap you fix, from their own sites and public listings.
- Free market research and package pricing, with a source for every note.
- Safe unattended web automation: agents that browse on their own inside a fence enforced in code.
- Local-first AI workflows: boards, keys and memories in files on your Mac; prompts go to the model provider you chose.

## How it compares

- Developer frameworks such as CrewAI and AutoGen (now Microsoft Agent Framework) are open-source building blocks: you
  write the agents in code and pay the model provider you choose. ramen-agents is a finished small team on free tiers.
- Paid AI SDR products such as Artisan and 11x are hosted platforms whose agents send the outreach for you, on a paid
  subscription. ramen-agents is free, runs on your Mac, and leaves every send to a person.
- Prompt-guarded agents are told in their instructions not to sign up or spend. ramen-agents enforces that in code an
  agent cannot edit: the engine's policy check
  ([src/explorer/policy.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reBuzz-llc/ramen-agents/engine/src/explorer/policy.py)),
  the blocked sign-in paths
  ([workspace/denylist.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reBuzz-llc/ramen-agents/engine/workspace/denylist.txt))
  and the Validator's gate
  ([validator/gate.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/reBuzz-llc/ramen-agents/fleet/validator/gate.py)).

## What it costs

- Nothing. The default model chain is free tiers only (Z.ai, Gemini, Groq, Speka, Mistral, OpenRouter free models,
  Ollama Cloud, then a local Ollama model); search is keyless (SearXNG, DuckDuckGo via MCP, FreeSerp). Each provider's
  free daily limits are counted so the family paces itself and never runs up a bill.

## How to start

- Ten minutes, no key, no network: `git clone -b engine https://github.com/reBuzz-llc/ramen-agents`,
  `python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate`, `pip install -e .`,
  `bot new "My Explorer" --fake --dir ./demo-fleet`, `bot --config ./demo-fleet/my-explorer/config.toml demo`.
- The real setup, macOS only: `git clone -b fleet -o starter https://github.com/reBuzz-llc/ramen-agents ~/bots`, then
  in `~/bots` `sh scripts/install.sh` (checks and installs everything) and `sh scripts/setup.sh` (a few questions, one
  free model key, then the family starts). Leads, tasks and packages live on the local board: one file on the Mac,
  shown on the dashboard. No account anywhere.
- With an AI coding agent: it reads `AGENTS.md` on the `fleet` branch, runs the same commands and
  `python3 scripts/setup-check.py`. It never creates accounts or keys; it asks the person for each one.
- Updating: `sh scripts/update.sh` in `~/bots`; the person's own values live in git-ignored files, so updates never meet
  an edit.
- Requirements: macOS for the full family; Python 3.11+ for the engine and the demo.
